body:
## Verdict

No files were edited; this was static review plus code reading. I found **no memory-unsafety or direct panic** in `src/` (core is `#![no_std]`, `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]`, and contains no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`), but there are several **P1** security/contract violations and a long tail of **P2** correctness/rigor gaps. No **P0** survived: nothing gives code execution or UB from wire input without host cooperation.

---

## P1 findings

**P1-1 — Wire parser has no depth guard; limits are applied only after the whole tree/doc is allocated (plan violation + DoS).**
`crates/rich-editor-auy/src/wire/json_parser.rs:44-57,59-105` (`value`→`object`/`array` recursion, no depth counter), `src/wire/parser.rs:58,127-138` (`decode_block` recursion, `Doc::new` only at the end), `src/model/doc.rs:80-117` (only `max_doc_bytes`/`max_nodes`), `src/lib.rs:44-60` (`max_depth: u16` is declared and **never read anywhere**).
Scenario: `"[" * 200_000` (a few hundred KB) drives ~200k recursive frames → stack overflow/abort in the CLI and a WASM trap in browsers; nested input also reaches `count_descendants`, `a11y_tree`, `validate_a11y`, `to_json` before anything is rejected. This directly contradicts `plan/04_arquitetura.md:636` (“`parse` valida limites antes de alocar”) and the `max_depth` contract. Fix: count depth inside `Parser::value`/`decode_block` and return `ParseError`/`LimitError` at `max_depth`; enforce `Doc::new` depth; add a regression test with depth > limit.
Missing test: no test feeds a deep/hostile document (only round-trip in `tests/smoke.rs`).

**P1-2 — Duplicate-key detection is O(n²) over attacker-controlled objects (DoS).**
`src/wire/json_parser.rs:70` — `members.iter().any(|(name, _)| *name == key)` for every member.
Scenario: ~1 MB of distinct keys (`{"k0":0,"k1":0,...}`) causes ~10⁹ string comparisons; a single unauthenticated parse can stall a worker for tens of seconds (worse in WASM). The doc target is ~15 ms/MB (`DIVERGENCES.md` item D). Fix: sort-then-dedup or a `BTreeSet`/last-key check (keys are only used via linear `get`, so a sorted `Box<[(Box<str>, JsonValue)]>` + binary search is also cheaper).

**P1-3 — `StepMap::map_pos` returns `None` for any position after a shrinking range (I15 violation).**
`src/step/map.rs:85-88`: `let delta = range.new_len.checked_sub(range.old_len)?` — for a deletion `new_len < old_len` this is `None`, so every position strictly after the deleted/replaced range fails to map.
`src/state/selection.rs:107,115-116,120` then silently falls back to the *old* position (`unwrap_or(pos)`), producing a selection outside the new document after `delete`/paste-over.
Repro shape: delete `1..3` from a 10-byte block, map `Pos(5)` → `None` instead of `Pos(3)`. `plan/04:482` (I15) requires mapping never leave the result doc; a stale caret is out of bounds. Fix: compute `current - old_len + new_len` with checked subtract/add (or saturating) rather than `checked_sub`; propagate mapping failure in `Selection::map` instead of swallowing it.
Missing test: `grep` finds **no** mapping test anywhere (`map_pos`/`StepMap`/`Mapping` are untested).

**P1-4 — Inversion is not exact: undo loses formatting and can remove/add marks that existed before (I14 violation).**
`src/step/invert.rs:47-58` + `123-170`: a textual `Replace` inverse is built from `text_between`, which collects only run **text** (`out.push_str(slice)`); marks are discarded. Deleting bold text and undoing restores plain text.
`src/step/invert.rs:60-68`: `AddMark`→`RemoveMark` and `RemoveMark`→`AddMark` are context-free. If the mark was already present, `apply` is content-identical but still recorded with an inverse that strips it on undo (and vice versa).
Both are reachable through `command::delete_selection` / `command::toggle_mark` + `EditorState::undo`. `plan/04:481` (I14) requires `invert` to reproduce the original document. Fix: snapshot the removed runs (marks included) as a `Fragment` for the inverse, and make mark inverses depend on the pre-state (no-op inverse when the mark set already matches).
Missing test: `tests/editing.rs` only exercises plain text; no mark/undo or invert property test exists.

**P1-5 — Wire decode bypasses schema validation; `validate` CLI and PHP `Validator` report “ok” for structurally invalid docs.**
`src/wire/parser.rs:58-90,108-125,127-138`: `decode_attrs` never calls `Schema::validate_attrs`, `decode_block` never checks `content_allows`, and `decode_doc` never checks `doc_allows`. `decode_value` (`src/wire/attrs.rs:56-70`) ignores `AttrType::Int { min, max }` and never enforces `required`.
Concrete: `{"type":"doc","content":[{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":99}}]}` and `{"type":"doc","content":[{"type":"image"}]}` parse successfully; `{"type":"doc","content":[]}` violates `block+`. `cli/src/main.rs:35-46` prints `ok` for all of them because it only calls `from_json`, and `Doc::validate` is called **only from tests** (`tests/smoke.rs:59`, `tests/validation.rs:43`).
This contradicts the `Validator` contract in `plan/09_frontend-e-referencias.md:188` (“relatório do CLI (violações, offsets)”) and makes the CLI's `validate`/`a11y` the only Rust-side gate, neither of which runs `Doc::validate`. Fix: validate attrs (type + range + required) and content expressions during decode, or have CLI `validate` run `Doc::validate` and report `DocIssue`s. Add tests for each invariant reached through the wire.
(If decode is intentionally syntax-only, then the CLI must be renamed/behave accordingly — as-is the name and PHP API are misleading.)

**P1-6 — DOM adapter copies untrusted `href`/`src` verbatim into the DOM → `javascript:` XSS.**
`packages/ts/packages/dom/render.ts:52-59` and `121-122` call `setAttribute("href", node.href)` / `setAttribute("src", node.src)` with no scheme check. `href` comes from the `link` mark, declared as `AttrType::Str` (`src/schema/preset.rs:66`), and from wire JSON with no URL policy (`src/a11y/build.rs:143-146`, `mark_attr` at 300-306). Text/markup injection is **not** possible (`createTextNode`/`textContent`, fixed tag whitelist), but `<a href="javascript:alert(document.domain)">…` executes on click; `data:`/`vbscript:` are equally accepted.
Plan/09 (`:190`) only requires an explicit sanitization policy for the optional HTML renderer and `:382` says sanitization is never the core's; this adapter is a renderer and has no policy. Fix: allowlist `http(s)`/`mailto`/relative/`#` (and `blob:`/`data:` only for media if intended) before setting `href`/`src`, and add a `javascript:` regression test.
Missing test: `packages/ts/packages/dom/render_test.ts` only asserts `https://example.test`.

**P1-7 — Schema fingerprint omits semantic declaration fields, so different schemas share a fingerprint.**
`src/schema/builder.rs:227-280`: the hashed text includes node `name/kind/content/groups/marks/inline` and mark `name/id/inclusive` + attr `id/name/kind/required`. It **omits** `NodeSpec.atom/defining/isolating/a11y`, `MarkSpec.excludes/groups/a11y`, `DocSpec.a11y`, and `AttrSpec.default`.
Consequence: `Envelope::from_json` (`src/wire/envelope.rs:72-80`) accepts an envelope as compatible after only the fingerprint check, even though `atom`/`a11y`/excludes changes alter decoding/validation semantics. That defeats the “detect wrong schema before loading” contract (`plan/04:571-574`). Fix: hash every semantic field (or hash the canonical serialized declaration), and add a golden test proving a change to `atom`/`a11y`/`excludes` changes the fingerprint.

---

## P2 findings

**P2-1 — Run/block limits are misapplied or dead; parser accepts runs > `MAX_RUN_BYTES`.**
`src/wire/parser.rs:118` calls `normalize(options.limits.max_block_text_bytes)` — 1 MiB by default — as the *run* ceiling, while `src/model/text.rs:20` defines `MAX_RUN_BYTES = 4096` and `src/model/validate.rs` flags I4 above it, and `src/step/text_edit.rs:89,157,252` splits at `MAX_RUN_BYTES`. A wire doc can therefore contain a 1 MiB text node and canonicalize differently from the same content produced by edits; `max_block_text_bytes` is also never checked as a per-block total, and `max_runs_per_block` (`src/lib.rs:56`) is never read. Contradicts `plan/04:185-186,471,555-557`. Fix: split at `MAX_RUN_BYTES`, reject blocks over `max_block_text_bytes`, enforce `max_runs_per_block`.
Missing test: no wire test for run ceiling/normalization (I4).

**P2-2 — `max_attrs_per_node`, `max_mark_attrs`, `max_attr_string_bytes` are declared and never enforced; attributes are outside the doc byte budget.**
`src/lib.rs:54-60` (fields), `src/model/doc.rs:80-117` (size sums only `block.size()`, which excludes attrs), `src/wire/attrs.rs:17-56` (no count/length checks). A doc-root `lang`/`dir` or a mark/atom attr can carry arbitrarily long strings (bounded only by input and `u32`), and `{"type":"doc","attrs":{"lang":"<64 MB>"}}` is accepted because the doc size is 0. Fix: enforce the three limits in `decode_attrs`/`Attrs::new`, and count attr bytes in `Doc::new` or the wire budget.

**P2-3 — `decode_ref` silently drops invalid `node`/`version` and accepts unordered fragments (lossy import, I16).**
`src/wire/attrs.rs:81-95`: `.and_then(NodeId::new)` / `.and_then(VersionTag::new)` turn an invalid/oversized value into `None` instead of an error, and `Range::new(Pos(start), Pos(end))` accepts `start > end`. `Doc::validate` only checks that the value is `AttrValue::Ref`, not its shape. An attacker can strip a reference's version pin or node anchor and the document still validates. Contradicts AGENTS contract 7 and I16. Fix: error on present-but-invalid `node`/`version`; reject `start > end`.

**P2-4 — `decode_block` silently discards inline data when an inline node appears in block position.**
`src/wire/parser.rs:127-138` recurses with `decode_block` for any mixed container; `decode_inline`'s `text` branch (`:147-158`) is bypassed, so `{"type":"bullet_list","content":[{"type":"text","text":"x"}]}` decodes to an empty text block, silently losing `"x"`. Also `{"type":"bullet_list"}` (no content) becomes a **text** block of kind `bullet_list`. Fix: reject non-inline children in block position / text nodes outside inline position instead of dropping data.

**P2-5 — TS `Document.fromEnvelope` validates nothing and ignores the schema argument.**
`packages/ts/packages/core/mod.ts:64-72,120-125`: `_schema` is unused, `JSON.parse` rejects non-JSON with a raw `SyntaxError`, only `doc !== undefined` is checked, and envelope `format`/`version`/`schema_fingerprint` are ignored, unlike Rust `Envelope::from_json` (verifies all three) and PHP `Document::fromBytes` (verifies all three). Same bytes are accepted/rejected differently across SDKs — inconsistent validation of the same transport. Fix: parse and verify `format`/`version`/`schema_fingerprint` (against `fingerprint()`) before decoding `doc`, and map `SyntaxError` to `DocumentError`.

**P2-6 — PHP accepts a JSON *array* as `doc` and mixes exception types.**
`packages/php/src/Document.php:22-29`: `is_array($json['doc'] ?? null)` is true for a JSON array (`"doc":[]`), despite the error text “doc object”; only the envelope fields are then checked. So `{"format":"rich-editor-auy","version":1,"schema_fingerprint":"<64hex>","doc":[]}` is accepted as a valid envelope. Also `json_decode(..., JSON_THROW_ON_ERROR)` throws `JsonException`, not the documented `InvalidArgumentException`, so callers catching the documented type miss parse failures. (`plan/09:186-188` leaves schema/normalization out of scope, so the unchecked doc *body* is by contract; the `doc` shape check is not.) Fix: require `is_array($doc) && array_is_list($doc) === false` and `$doc['type'] === 'doc'`; wrap `JsonException`.

**P2-7 — Rigor gates are fiction: the `a11y` gate runs zero tests and is absent from CI; miri uses the wrong target; fuzz/apply and property tests don't exist.**
`Makefile:20-21` runs `cargo test -p rich-editor-auy --locked a11y`, but no test name or test binary contains `a11y` and `src/` has no `#[cfg(test)]` modules ⇒ zero tests run, exit 0. `.github/workflows/ci.yml:27-28` runs `test` and `visits` but **never** the `a11y` target. `Makefile:54-55` and `ci.yml:64` run `--test smoke`, so `tests/miri_smoke.rs` is never run under miri (AGENTS §7 says `--test miri_smoke`). `fuzz/Cargo.toml` only defines `json_parse` (AGENTS §7 promises `apply_step`; `ci.yml:118` and `Makefile:57-58` only run `json_parse`). `crates/rich-editor-auy/Cargo.toml:22` has empty `[dev-dependencies]`; workspace deps dropped `proptest`/`serde_json`, so `plan/07` property/differential tests and AGENTS §8 (golden a11y, one case per `A11yCode`, proptest for normalize/map/serialize/apply-invert) do not exist. This violates plan/07's “each rule has a command that fails” and the a11y gate in AGENTS §6.15/§7. Fix: name a11y tests with `a11y` (or run a dedicated test binary), add the per-code/golden/a11y-tree tests, wire `a11y` into CI, fix the miri target, add `apply_step` fuzz, and restore proptest/serde_json differential tests.

**P2-8 — CLI reads unbounded stdin/files and has no input size cap.**
`cli/src/main.rs:26-30` (`io::stdin().read_to_string(&mut input)`), `:110` (`fs::read_to_string`) — the entire input is buffered before `from_json`, with no byte cap, so a slow/large stream is an OOM/DoS vector for a service wrapping the CLI (PHP `Validator` writes caller-supplied bytes into stdin). Fix: enforce `Limits::max_doc_bytes` (plus slack) while reading, e.g. `Read::take`.

**P2-9 — `toggle_mark` cannot remove marks.**
`crates/rich-editor-auy-wasm/src/lib.rs:106-115` always calls `add_mark`; `src/command/mod.rs:50-56` decides add/remove from `state.stored_marks()`, not from the marks actually present in the selected range. Toggling an existing bold run therefore re-adds it instead of clearing it. Fix: inspect the runs in the range (or add a real `toggle` step) and mirror it in WASM.

**P2-10 — `block_at` returns the last block for positions past the document; `SetNodeAttr` then silently edits it.**
`src/model/doc.rs:158-168`: `partition_point(...).saturating_sub(1)` never rejects `pos > doc.size()`; `src/step/apply.rs:252-259` (`locate`) relies on it, and `set_node_attr` (`:177-...`) then writes the attribute to the last block instead of returning `OutOfBounds`. Fix: `block_at` must return `None` when `pos > size` (or explicitly check in `locate`), and add a test.

**P2-11 — Select-all + insert/delete fails on structural tokens.**
`src/command/mod.rs:89-93` sets `Selection::text(Pos::ZERO, Pos(size))`; `insert_text`/`delete_selection` (`:16-47`) then queue a plain-text `Replace` covering block open/close tokens, which `src/step/apply.rs:84-88` rejects (`replace_structural_token`) or `text_edit::replace_text` rejects as out of range. So a whole-document selection cannot be replaced/deleted. Fix: map the selection to content-only ranges, or emit a structural `Replace`/`Slice` for token-spanning ranges; add an end-to-end test.

**P2-12 — Parser error locations are not localized.**
`src/wire/parser.rs:60,77,82,87,121,144,153,161,166` all report `offset: 0`; `:60` even derives the offset from `error.to_string().len()`. `ParseError` (`src/error/wire.rs:11-22`) has only `code/offset/path` — no line/column. `plan/04:578-579` requires offset + line/column + node path and “nada de ‘invalid JSON’ sem localização”. Fix: thread the current parser offset into structural errors and compute line/column on display; add tests asserting offsets.

**P2-13 — Parser is “strict” only partially and has no differential test.**
`src/wire/json_parser.rs:196-222` accepts JSON numbers with leading zeros (`01` → `1`; `text.parse::<i64>()` is lenient), while `:150-168` rejects valid JSON `\uD8xx\uDCxx` surrogate pairs (`char::from_u32` returns `None` for surrogates), so valid emoji escapes are unparseable. No test compares against a reference parser (the promised `serde_json` dev-dep is absent). Fix: enforce `0` or non-zero lead digit, decode surrogate pairs, and add the differential/property test.

---

## Answers to the five questions

**(1) Can parser input cause panic/DoS?**
No safe-Rust panic found: the core has no `unwrap`/`expect`/`panic!`/indexing and the parser uses `get` for every slice. But **DoS is credible and unmitigated**: unbounded recursion depth (stack overflow → abort/WASM trap), O(n²) duplicate-key scan, limits checked only after the full `JsonValue`/`Doc` is built, unbounded attribute strings, and unbounded CLI `read_to_string`. OOM also aborts. (`P1-1`, `P1-2`, `P2-1`, `P2-2`, `P2-8`.)

**(2) Can the DOM renderer inject markup/script or unsafe URL?**
Markup/script injection: **no** — `renderText` uses `createTextNode`/`textContent`, tags come from a fixed whitelist, and all values are set via attribute APIs. Unsafe URL: **yes** — untrusted `href`/`src` are copied verbatim to `<a>`/media elements, so `javascript:`/`data:`/`vbscript:` links execute on activation (`P1-6`). No `innerHTML` is used to render document content (only to save/restore the host in `mod.ts:30,65`).

**(3) Can PHP accept malformed envelopes?**
Partly. `Envelope::validate()` correctly enforces `format == "rich-editor-auy"`, `version == 1`, and 64 lowercase hex fingerprint, and `Document::fromBytes` requires JSON parsing to succeed. But the `doc` shape check is `is_array(...)`, which accepts a JSON list; a doc body that is not an object (`"doc":[]`) passes; extra/unknown fields are ignored; and `JsonException` escapes instead of the documented `InvalidArgumentException`. Schema/normalization of the doc body being unchecked is **by contract** per `plan/09:186-188`, so only the shape/exception issues are new (`P2-6`).

**(4) Can the CLI disclose or overwrite paths?**
It never writes to the filesystem (no output files, no temp files; all output is stdout/stderr), so **no overwrite**. `diff` reads exactly the caller-supplied argv paths and echoes the path in error messages — that is a deliberate diff interface, not traversal from content; but any service that forwards untrusted paths into `diff` would grant arbitrary file reads to the process's privilege. `validate`/`format`/`a11y*` read stdin with no size cap (`P2-8`).

**(5) Any `unsafe` outside allowed test/glue?**
Core is `#![forbid(unsafe_code)]` (`src/lib.rs:16-17`); no `unsafe` in `crates/rich-editor-auy-wasm`, `-testkit`, or `-macros`. `unsafe` appears only in the core's own integration tests — `crates/rich-editor-auy/tests/alloc.rs:3,23-52` and `tests/memory.rs:2,20-49` (counting `GlobalAlloc`, each with `SAFETY` and `allow(reason)`). `plan/07:§3.1` enumerates testkit/fuzz/bench/wasm as the allowed places, not the core's integration tests, so this is a minor policy deviation, not a soundness risk.

---

## Coverage

- Reviewed: all of `crates/rich-editor-auy/src/{wire,model,pos,step,state,a11y,error,schema,input,command,math,motion,lib}.rs`, `crates/rich-editor-auy/tests/*`, `crates/rich-editor-auy-wasm/src/lib.rs`, `crates/rich-editor-auy-{testkit,macros}/src/lib.rs`, `cli/src/main.rs`, `packages/ts/packages/{core,dom,schema}`, `packages/php/src/*`, `fuzz/`, `Makefile`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `scripts/check_zero_style.sh`, `examples/host/index.html`, `examples/php/roundtrip.php`.
- No commands/tests were executed (review-only, static evidence); recommended gates for the main agent: `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `cargo test -p rich-editor-auy --locked a11y` (verify it actually selects tests), `cargo +nightly fuzz run json_parse`, and the Deno/PHP suite.
